Q: How to average multiple files across groups A:

If you don't mind using some data.tables, this should work:

library(data.table) ## concise, fast data manipulation
library(vroom) ## for fast bulk CSV import

## extend your group lookup table from `data.frame` to class `data.table`:
scang <- as.data.table(scang)


## ingest all your scan data into one large `data.table`:
scan_data <- 
    vroom(list.files("/path/to/scans/", pattern = ".csv", full.names = TRUE),
          id = "B" ## store full CSV filepath as column B
          ) |>
    as.data.table()


## set row index per input CSV filename (in column B) to make sure
## we dont mix up the rows later on:
scan_data[, row_index := 1:.N, by = B]



scang[
    ## left join to scan data on column B:
    scan_data, on = "B"
][ 
    ## calculate averages for numeric columns
    ## grouping by A and row index
    ## (`.SD` denotes user-defined SubSet of rows and columns)
   ,
    lapply(.SD, \(xs) ifelse(is.numeric(xs), mean(xs), first(xs))),
    by = c("A", "row_index")
][
    !is.na(C), ## skip if no outfile name is given in C
    fwrite(.SD, first(C)), ## store SubData under filename in C
    by = A
]

Make sure input file paths stored in scang and those returned by list.files match.

Q: Only show the decimal point if the floating point component is not .00 sprintf/printf A:

If you're using rails, you can use rails' NumberHelper methods: http://api.rubyonrails.org/classes/ActionView/Helpers/NumberHelper.html

number_with_precision(13.001, precision: 2, strip_insignificant_zeros: true)
# => 13
number_with_precision(13.005, precision: 2, strip_insignificant_zeros: true)
# => 13.01

Be careful, because precision means all digits after decimal point in this case.

Q: TypeError: Cannot read property 'access_token' of undefined A:

Some where in your code (not in the file you gave) you are accessing access_token somewhat like this: some-object.access_token

But, some-object might be null as well. So to avoid the error you could use optional chaining like this: some-object?.access_token

The question mark "?" is for the optional chaining. it will first check if "some-object" is present or not and then it will try to access "access_token"
